preferential exclusion of weakly interacting excipients from the protein surface is linearly related with their concentration in solution.

preferential interactions of trehalse and L-arginin.HCl with the protein molecules studied in this study are linearly related to excipient concentration in the case of the former and non-linear in the case of latter.

the preferential interactions and the resultant effect of trehalose on the self-association and viscosity of IgG1 monocloals depends on their surface characteristics, whereas L-arginine and sodium chloride have similar effect on the same properties of IgG1 molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with

elucidating the molecular mechanisms governing the effect of excipients on the behavior of protein molecules in aqueous solutions, with the goal of developing a rational basis for excipient design in biopharmaceuticals.

the characterization of excipients in terms of their preferential interactions with proteins, and their effect on the self-association, viscosity, aggregation and precipitation behavior of mAb formulations.
the development of a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms governing excipients-mediated stabilization of mAbs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the preferential interactions and hence the effect of excipients on the self-association and aggregation kinetics of mAb molecules is dependent upon the net charge and the hydrophobicity of the mAb molecules.
preferential interactions govern excipient-mediated stabilization.
the preferential interactions are not the sole determinant of the effect of excipients on protein stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the preferential interactions between the excipient and the surface of a protein molecule is the primary factor governing the effect of excipients on the equilibrium and kinetic behavior of proteins in solution.
the effect of excipients on the stability of mAbs is a complex interplay between the nature of excipient and protein surface.
trehalose is the best excipient for stabilizing IgG1 monocloal antibodies, whereas NaCl and L arginine.HCl are the worst.
The main takeaway from our work is that
excipients that preferentially interact with the protein surface are likely to have the greatest potential to stabilize the protein molecules against aggregation.

the effect of excipients on the self-association behavior of mAb molecules can be predicted from their preferential interactions with the protein surface, which in turn depends upon the surface hydrophobic and charge properties of the protein.
the preferential interactions between excipients and mAbs are a function of the surface properties of the mAb, and not just the net charge of the protein molecule.
